newsitem.title: GERMANY: Sixt sees 1997 profit rising 35-40 pct.
newsitem.headline: Sixt sees 1997 profit rising 35-40 pct.

text.p: German rental car group Sixt AG said on Friday it expected 1997 profit from ordinary activities to rise 35 to 40 percent.
The company also said first quarter profit from ordinary activities rose 49.2 percent to 9.9 million marks.

"In view of the results of the first quarter, the management board expects for the full year a rise in group sales of 25 percent and an overproportional profit increase of 35 to 40 percent," the company said in a statement.
Sixt also said it expected to pay an unchanged dividend of 14 marks per share with a bonus of 3.50 marks.
First-quarter sales rose 23 percent to 622 million marks.

Its rental unit saw first-quarter sales rise 32 percent to 203 million marks, while its auto sales operation had a revenue increase of 17 percent, to 378.7 million marks. Sixt Leasing AG sales in the quarter rose 61 percent to 36.5 million marks.
To meet rising demand, the company invested 600 million marks in 19,000 new vehicles in the first quarter.
-- Neal Boudette, Bonn Newsroom, + 49-228 26097150 (c) Reuters Limited 1997
